_: The King's sheet and his family (royal_sheet.gd; CK3's ruler window), opened from the bar's heading. Each line's words; {name}, {age}, {traits}, {house}, {how} are filled from /world royals (bridge royals.js). nature_tip: why his nature matters at court; regency: while a child is King; no_heir: with none; abdicate_tip: what stepping down does. trust: what his word is worth, by bands of the bridge's trust (0..1; the first whose above it clears): says on his sheet, pledge under a promise at court (the council's tone), low in red. stress: how he bears his rulings, by bands of royals.king.stress (from; the bridge's stress.high is 3): says on his sheet, grade the colour laid on his portrait.
none: The royal house is not yet known.
nature_tip: Lords of a like nature warm to him; those of the opposite nature cool. A new King is measured again by every lord.
regency: A child sits the throne. Until he comes of age the realm is held by a regent, and cold lords rise more readily.
no_heir: There is no heir. If the King dies so, the crown is up for the taking.
abdicate_tip: The heir is of age. The crown passes to him now, and every lord takes his measure afresh.
funeral: The great houses swore to the old King, not to this one. Old friends wait to be won again, and old grudges are half forgotten.

focus._: Who the King means to be (royal_sheet.gd _focus_row; bridge royals.js focus): head over the choice; tips by focus id; once under it; chosen ({focus}: its label from the bridge) once made; against: the tag under an answer that goes against it (event cards, court); trait_against ({trait}): a court answer against his own nature.
focus.head: Who he means to be

tips.war: A King of the sword. War will find him more often, and buying peace will gnaw at him.
tips.court: A King of his lords. Their quarrels will come to him more often, and a hard word to one will gnaw at him.
tips.faith: A King of the faith. The church and the poor will come to him more often, and cruelty will gnaw at him.
tips.coin: A King of the purse. Trade and the treasury will need him more often, and gold thrown away will gnaw at him.

focus.once: He chooses once. The realm will test him on it.
focus.chosen: He means to be remembered for {focus}.
focus.against: Against who he means to be: it will weigh on him.
focus.trait_against: Against his {trait} nature: it will weigh on him.

council._: The first council (royal_sheet.gd _first_council; CK3's opening: your ruler, your situation, your focus): once a reign, by_turn its first seasons, after seconds once the crowning has had its moment. The King first: crowned ({seat}, {season}) over his painted face (face: width, height), head ({name}) at head_size, age ({age}), nature ({traits}); then situation over the lines; friend, foe ({house}, {mood}); rival ({king}, {realm}, {edge}); chest ({crowns}); ok closes it.
council.head: King {name}
council.situation: The realm as you find it, Your Grace
council.rival: Beyond the {edge} border, {king} of {realm} watches the new King.

lord_loyalty.says: Wavering: another house could buy this loyalty.
Would sell {liege} for the right price.

lord_sheet._: A person's sheet (hero_view.gd; CK3's character window): a card over the realm. dim: the realm behind it (r, g, b, a); width of the card; face: the painted portrait (width, height).

lord_holdings._: A lord's sheet, what he holds (hero_view.gd _holdings; bridge /world cities, vassals): head; towns ({towns}) and sworn ({houses}) for a great house's lord; vassal ({house}, {town}, {liege}) for a sworn lord.
lord_holdings.head: Holds

lost._: A crown town lost (royal_sheet.gd _lost; casebook, Defeat is a chapter): head ({town}), the Hand's line, vow ({town}) and vowed: the King swears to take it back; look, let_go: the other buttons; kept ({town}): the news when a sworn town is the crown's again.
lost.head: {town} is lost
lost.hand: The Hand: “Every King loses a town, Your Grace. The ones the realm remembers take it back.”
lost.vowed: The King swears before the court to take back {town}. The realm will remember whether he does.
lost.kept: The King's vow is kept: {town} flies the crown's banner again.

rising._: A lord's rebellion, the Hand's warning at court (royal_sheet.gd on_chronicle; bridge characters.js chronicle kind rebellion, fe1500d0): head ({name}: the house), warn: the Hand's line, look: the button that shows the rebel's seat, ok: the one that closes the card.
rising.head: {name} rises against the crown
rising.warn: The Hand: “Call your host home and look to the walls, Your Grace. They are on the road already.”

pledge_tag: Your word. Kept, it is remembered warmly; broken, bitterly.
raid_news: Raiders out of {from} make for the King's {work} at {town}. Send men, or lose it.
news_broken: The King's word is broken: {text}. They will remember it.

trust.says: His word is good. The houses take it at its face.
trust.pledge: Your word. Kept, it is remembered warmly; broken, bitterly.

trust.says: His word is doubted. A promise warms them less than it did.
trust.pledge: Your word, Your Grace. They have heard it before, and weigh it.

trust.says: His word is wind. The houses hear a promise and wait to see it done.
trust.pledge: Your word? The Hand would not lean on it; the houses have learned not to.

stress.says: He sleeps badly. What he has ruled against his own nature is wearing him down, and it may shorten his days.
Some of his rulings sit ill with him.

rest._: Easing the King's mind on his sheet (bridge royals.js rest: the gold, ease and seasons are the bridge's): each kind's button word, its hover line and what is said when done; again ({n}) and poor on a locked one.
rest.risk: One hunt in {n} ends with the King carried home hurt.
rest.head: Ease his mind

hunt.label: Hunt
hunt.tip: A day in the royal forest eases him. Once a year; a fall from the saddle is not unknown.
hunt.done: The King rides out to hunt.

feast.label: Feast
feast.tip: A feast in the great hall eases him, and every great house warms a little. Once a year.
feast.done: The great hall is made ready for a feast.

pilgrimage.label: Pilgrimage
pilgrimage.tip: Barefoot to the old shrine: it eases him most, and the pious lords warm to him. Once in two years.
pilgrimage.done: The King sets out on pilgrimage.

rest.again: Not again so soon: in {n} seasons.
rest.poor: The treasury holds too little for this.
